Replay

Party menus and durable enrollment

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Invites and host migrationConfiguration and profilesParty checkpoint publication

Create or join a Replay Cavecrawl party through the room service, which enrolls trusted members and coordinates which process may host. This flow supplies member IDs and control keys instead of requiring players to configure them. With REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_SERVICE configured, the menu shows Create party, Join party, Rejoin recent party, and Copy party invite. Without it, the existing solo/LAN menu and preconfigured fixtures remain.

Creating or joining first persists the exact enrollment request. A successful credential becomes usable only after its storage receipt. Native macOS/Linux uses the optional private SQLite client store; browsers use IndexedDB. Records are scoped by the exact service URL and room ID. New parties get new records; existing credentials are not overwritten.

A small recent-party reference is stored separately with its own compare-and-swap. It changes only after the enrollment request is durable, and before that request is sent. A failed/conflicting reference stops the attempt. Rejoin recent party loads the exact stored request or credential, then performs normal challenged process registration. A missing/corrupt record does not create a replacement identity. Joining again with an invite also finds that room's existing credential.

Invites and host migration#

Cavecrawl issues one co-op invite with SEATS - 1 uses. Its secret is derived with HMAC from the creator's persisted claim, exact service URL, room/content, role, use count and index zero. Retrying after restart reproduces the same capability and issuance parameters. It does not issue extra uses, revive a revoked invite, or disclose the creator's secret to recipients. New indices are explicit new invitations, not automatic retry behavior. This version does not expose invite rotation/revocation controls.

The invite grants trusted co-op membership, including permission to host and receive complete authority backups. The menu states that invited friends can keep playing if the host disconnects. Competitive games must choose their own admission policy; dedicated public creation/trusted-player invites remain refused by the backend.

Room's opt-in automatic successor mode selects a connected eligible member in stable seat order, checking the authenticated roster, token, current incarnation, hosting/trust permission and infrastructure requirement where applicable. Revoking an active target's eligibility stops further backup publication. Disconnected targets retain their last inspectable receipt until replacement. Existing explicit successor configuration remains available.

The shared Party API manages setup and storage, also used by Scrapyard. Existing Cavecrawl enrollment and recent-room keys are preserved. An unavailable invite no longer prevents an already authorized creator from using its stored credential; the UI reports the invitation separately.

The menu flow uses the normal checkpoint/lease machinery. Tests exercise planned handoff with zero lost ticks, preserved guest loot, and a departed host reopening its profile with a fresh incarnation and the same invite. Leave closes the Room; a surviving prepared successor follows the abrupt recovery policy. If every participant exits, credentials alone cannot restore gameplay. The service can restore only progress explicitly published through the checkpoint flow below.

Configuration and profiles#

Setting Purpose
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_SERVICE / browser room_service Provisioning/control/signaling service URL
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_LOCAL=1 / room_local=1 Explicit loopback WS development mode
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_CA Optional native certificate authority for a private verified TLS service
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOMS_DB Native credential database, default isolated user://rooms.sqlite3
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_ADDRESS / room_address Advertised gameplay endpoint host, default 127.0.0.1
REPLAY_CAVE_PORT / port Native gameplay port, default 49422
REPLAY_CAVE_ICE_JSON Native RTC deployment configuration, when using an RTC extension
REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_RELAY=1 / room_relay=1 Obtain and refresh credentials from the room service

Browser hosts can supply globalThis.replayIceConfig before Godot starts. It is not a query parameter. Actual relay-only UDP/TCP tests cover this party flow; see ICE deployment settings for scope and limits.

Native clients on the same machine need different gameplay ports and different credential databases when representing different players. For different machines, advertise addresses reachable by the other peers; a loopback address is local only. This example does not provide automatic NAT traversal for ENet. Browser RTC uses the service's challenged signaling; public relay/ICE deployment remains work.

The browser menu can be opened with room_service and explicit local-development parameters; the invite itself is pasted into the game, not placed in a URL. Browser profiles represent separate players. Same-origin tabs sharing storage reuse the same room credential, and process registration applies the existing live-instance rules. Display-name preferences and local solo saves remain separate.

The party remains bound to its original service URL. Moving services, retiring profiles, forgotten recent-room records, invitation rotation and all-participants- gone gameplay recovery need explicit workflows; no identity or authority fallback is inferred. Original Cavecrawl, original Scrapyard and the Kit framework remain separately runnable.

See native/browser evidence and the library enrollment contract.

Party checkpoint publication#

An online host can request a durable service checkpoint through F5/the save action or Store party checkpoint. Set REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS=10000 (browser parameter room_checkpoint_ms=10000) for automatic publication. The default is manual; valid automatic intervals are 1–120 seconds. The configured service must support Cavecrawl checkpoints. Solo/local saves stay separate.

The Room driver handles status lookup, immutable capture, authenticated upload and lost-reply recovery while leases and live backups continue. The stored tick is a durable snapshot boundary; work after it is not claimed as saved. An interruption may leave the outcome uncertain until a fresh status check.

Rejoin recent party can recover that stored progress after everyone leaves. It joins a live host when one exists; otherwise a trusted returning player downloads the saved world and obtains a newer authority epoch before play resumes. Missing, invalid or too-old saves show a recovery error and retry option instead of starting an empty replacement world. The service's configured rollback limit still applies. Native and browser tests resume the saved cave, admit a new guest, execute new loot actions and store the continued game. See Room restoration and the remaining M5 plan. See the Room API.
